sanskrit: tataḥ krodhasamāviṣṭaṃ saṃrabdhaṃ tam upāgatam ahaṃ prasādayāṃ cakre bhrātaraṃ priyakāmyayā
english: Then, out of desire for his good will, I sought to placate my brother who had come upon me seized with anger and agitation.

sanskrit: diṣṭyāsi kuśalī prāpto nihataś ca tvayā ripuḥ anāthasya hi me nāthas tvam eko 'nāthanandanaḥ
english: "By good fortune you have returned safe, and the enemy has been slain by you; for me who was without a protector, you alone are my protector — the joy of one who had none."

sanskrit: idaṃ bahuśalākaṃ te pūrṇacandram ivoditam chatraṃ savālavyajanaṃ pratīcchasva mayodyatam
english: "Receive this royal parasol, raised aloft by me, adorned with many ribs, risen like a full moon, together with the yak-tail fans."

sanskrit: tvam eva rājā mānārhaḥ sadā cāhaṃ yathāpurā nyāsabhūtam idaṃ rājyaṃ tava niryātayāmy aham
english: "You alone are the king worthy of honour, and I am ever as before — I restore to you this kingdom that was held in trust."

sanskrit: mā ca roṣaṃ kṛthāḥ saumya mayi śatrunibarhaṇa yāce tvāṃ śirasā rājan mayā baddho 'yam añjaliḥ
english: "Do not be angry with me, gentle one, O destroyer of enemies; I beseech you, O king, with my head — these joined palms are folded by me."

sanskrit: balād asmi samāgamya mantribhiḥ puravāsibhiḥ rājabhāve niyukto 'haṃ śūnyadeśajigīṣayā
english: "I was forcibly brought together with the ministers and the citizens of the capital and installed in the royal office out of a desire to keep the kingdom from becoming masterless."

sanskrit: snigdham evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ māṃ sa tu nirbhartsya vānaraḥ dhik tvām iti ca mām uktvā bahu tat tad uvāca ha
english: But that monkey, despite my speaking to him with affection, reviled me and, saying "Shame on you," said many reproachful things.

sanskrit: prakṛtīś ca samānīya mantriṇaś caiva saṃmatān mām āha suhṛdāṃ madhye vākyaṃ paramagarhitam
english: Having gathered the subjects together and the respected ministers as well, he spoke to me in the midst of friends words that were most shameful.

sanskrit: viditaṃ vo yathā rātrau māyāvī sa mahāsuraḥ māṃ samāhvayata krūro yuddhākāṅkṣī sudurmatiḥ
english: "You know how that great demon, that trickster, that cruel and utterly wicked one who longed for battle, challenged me one night."

sanskrit: tasya tad garjitaṃ śrutvā niḥsṛto 'haṃ nṛpālayāt anuyātaś ca māṃ tūrṇam ayaṃ bhrātā sudāruṇaḥ
english: "Hearing that roar of his, I issued forth from the royal palace, and this harsh brother of mine followed swiftly behind me."

sanskrit: sa tu dṛṣṭvaiva māṃ rātrau sadvitīyaṃ mahābalaḥ prādravad bhayasaṃtrasto vīkṣyāvāṃ tam anudrutau anudrutas tu vegena praviveśa mahābilam
english: "That mighty one, seeing me accompanied by another in the night, fled in fear; we two gave chase, and he, being pursued, swiftly entered into the great cave."

sanskrit: taṃ praviṣṭaṃ viditvā tu sughoraṃ sumahad bilam ayam ukto 'tha me bhrātā mayā tu krūradarśanaḥ
english: "Knowing he had entered that most dreadful and vast cavern, I then addressed this brother of mine, fierce in aspect:"

sanskrit: ahatvā nāsti me śaktiḥ pratigantum itaḥ purīm biladvāri pratīkṣa tvaṃ yāvad enaṃ nihanmy aham
english: "'I have not the power to return to the city without slaying him — wait at the mouth of the cave until I have killed him.'"

sanskrit: sthito 'yam iti matvā tu praviṣṭo 'haṃ durāsadam taṃ ca me mārgamāṇasya gataḥ saṃvatsaras tadā
english: "Believing he would remain there, I entered that difficult lair; and while I was searching for him, a full year passed."

sanskrit: sa tu dṛṣṭo mayā śatrur anirvedād bhayāvahaḥ nihataś ca mayā tatra so 'suro bandhubhiḥ saha
english: "That fearsome enemy was finally found by me without despairing, and there he was slain by me along with his kinsmen."

sanskrit: tasyāsyāt tu pravṛttena rudhiraugheṇa tad bilam pūrṇam āsīd durākrāmaṃ stanatas tasya bhūtale
english: "That cave became filled with a flood of blood flowing from his mouth, impassable, while he rumbled upon the ground."

sanskrit: sūdayitvā tu taṃ śatruṃ vikrāntaṃ dundubheḥ sutam niṣkrāmann eva paśyāmi bilasya pihitaṃ mukham
english: "Having slain that valiant enemy, the son of Dundubhi, I saw even as I was coming out that the mouth of the cave was sealed shut."

sanskrit: vikrośamānasya tu me sugrīveti punaḥ punaḥ yadā prativaco nāsti tato 'haṃ bhṛśaduḥkhitaḥ
english: "As I called out again and again 'Sugrīva!' and there was no answer at all, I became exceedingly sorrowful."

sanskrit: pādaprahārais tu mayā bahuśas tad vidāritam tato 'haṃ tena niṣkramya yathā punar upāgataḥ
english: "I broke it open again and again with blows of my feet, then made my way out through it and returned home."

sanskrit: tatrānenāsmi saṃruddho rājyaṃ mārgayatātmanaḥ sugrīveṇa nṛśaṃsena vismṛtya bhrātṛsauhṛdam
english: "There, by this cruel Sugrīva, who sought the kingdom for himself and forgot the bond of brotherhood, I was barred from entry."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu māṃ tatra vastreṇaikena vānaraḥ tadā nirvāsayām āsa vālī vigatasādhvasaḥ
english: "Having spoken thus against me there, Vālī the monkey banished me, stripped of fear, with but a single garment."

sanskrit: tenāham apaviddhaś ca hṛtadāraś ca rāghava tadbhayāc ca mahīkṛtsnā krānteyaṃ savanārṇavā
english: "Cast out by him and robbed of my wife, O Rāghava, I have traversed this entire earth with its forests and oceans in fear of him."

sanskrit: ṛśyamūkaṃ girivaraṃ bhāryāharaṇaduḥkhitaḥ praviṣṭo 'smi durādharṣaṃ vālinaḥ kāraṇāntare
english: "Anguished by the abduction of my wife, I entered the foremost of mountains, Ṛśyamūka, which is impregnable, by reason of another circumstance concerning Vālī."

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ vairānukathanaṃ mahat anāgasā mayā prāptaṃ vyasanaṃ paśya rāghava
english: "All this great tale of the enmity has been told to you — behold, O Rāghava, the calamity that has befallen me though I am innocent."

sanskrit: vālinas tu bhayārtasya sarvalokābhayaṃkara kartum arhasi me vīra prasādaṃ tasya nigrahāt
english: "O hero who brings safety to all the worlds, you should grant me your grace, who am stricken with fear of Vālī, through his suppression."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa tejasvī dharmajño dharmasaṃhitam vacanaṃ vaktum ārebhe sugrīvaṃ prahasann iva
english: When thus addressed, that splendid one, the knower of dharma, began to speak words consonant with righteousness to Sugrīva, smiling gently.

sanskrit: amoghāḥ sūryasaṃkāśā mameme niśitāḥ śarāḥ tasmin vālini durvṛtte patiṣyanti ruṣānvitāḥ
english: "These sharp arrows of mine, bright as the sun, unfailing, will fall upon that wicked Vālī filled with my wrath."

sanskrit: yāvat taṃ na hi paśyeyaṃ tava bhāryāpahāriṇam tāvat sa jīvet pāpātmā vālī cāritradūṣakaḥ
english: "Only until I set eyes upon him who stole your wife does that vile-souled Vālī, that defiler of conduct, continue to live."

sanskrit: ātmānumānāt paśyāmi magnaṃ tvāṃ śokasāgare tvām ahaṃ tārayiṣyāmi kāmaṃ prāpsyasi puṣkalam
english: "Judging by my own experience, I see you plunged in an ocean of grief; I will carry you across, and you shall attain every abundance."

sanskrit: rāmasya vacanaṃ śrutvā harṣapauruṣavardhanam sugrīvaḥ pūjayāṃ cakre rāghavaṃ praśaśaṃsa ca
english: Hearing Rāma's words, which heightened both joy and valour, Sugrīva honoured the Rāghava and praised him.

sanskrit: asaṃśayaṃ prajvalitais tīkṣṇair marmātigaiḥ śaraiḥ tvaṃ daheḥ kupito lokān yugānta iva bhāskaraḥ
english: "Without doubt, with your blazing, sharp arrows that pierce vital spots, you could, when angered, burn the worlds, like the sun at the end of an age."

sanskrit: vālinaḥ pauruṣaṃ yat tad yac ca vīryaṃ dhṛtiś ca yā tan mamaikamanāḥ śrutvā vidhatsva yadanantaram
english: "Having heard with one-pointed mind what prowess, what valour, and what resolve Vālī possesses, decide thereafter what is to be done."

sanskrit: samudrāt paścimāt pūrvaṃ dakṣiṇād api cottaram krāmaty anudite sūrye vālī vyapagataklamaḥ
english: "Before the sun has risen, Vālī strides — from the western ocean to the eastern, from the southern to the northern — without weariness."

sanskrit: agrāṇy āruhya śailānāṃ śikharāṇi mahānty api ūrdhvam utkṣipya tarasā pratigṛhṇāti vīryavān
english: "Having ascended the peaks and great summits of mountains, that valiant one hurls them upward with force and catches them again."

sanskrit: bahavaḥ sāravantaś ca vaneṣu vividhā drumāḥ vālinā tarasā bhagnā balaṃ prathayatātmanaḥ
english: "Many sturdy trees of various kinds in the forests have been snapped by Vālī with force as he displays his strength."

sanskrit: mahiṣo dundubhir nāma kailāsaśikharaprabhaḥ balaṃ nāgasahasrasya dhārayām āsa vīryavān
english: "There was a buffalo named Dundubhi, brilliant as the peak of Kailāsa, who possessed the strength of a thousand elephants, so valiant was he."

sanskrit: vīryotsekena duṣṭātmā varadānāc ca mohitaḥ jagāma sa mahākāyaḥ samudraṃ saritāṃ patim
english: "Intoxicated by excess of might and deluded by the boon he had received, that great-bodied, evil-souled one went to the ocean, lord of rivers."

sanskrit: ūrmimantam atikramya sāgaraṃ ratnasaṃcayam mama yuddhaṃ prayaccheti tam uvāca mahārṇavam
english: "Surpassing the wave-crested ocean, treasure-laden, he addressed the great sea: 'Give me battle!'"

sanskrit: tataḥ samudro dharmātmā samutthāya mahābalaḥ abravīd vacanaṃ rājann asuraṃ kālacoditam
english: "Then the ocean, righteous-souled and mighty, rising up, spoke these words to that demon driven on by fate, O king:"

sanskrit: samartho nāsmi te dātuṃ yuddhaṃ yuddhaviśārada śrūyatām abhidhāsyāmi yas te yuddhaṃ pradāsyati
english: "'I am not capable of giving you battle, O master of warfare; hear, I shall tell you who will give you battle.'"

sanskrit: śailarājo mahāraṇye tapasviśaraṇaṃ param śaṃkaraśvaśuro nāmnā himavān iti viśrutaḥ
english: "'There is the king of mountains in the great forest, the supreme refuge of ascetics, the father-in-law of Śaṃkara, renowned by the name Himavān.'"

sanskrit: guhā prasravaṇopeto bahukandaranirjharaḥ sa samarthas tava prītim atulāṃ kartum āhave
english: "'Possessed of caverns and springs, full of many gorges and cascades — he is capable of giving you matchless satisfaction in combat.'"

sanskrit: taṃ bhītam iti vijñāya samudram asurottamaḥ himavadvanam āgacchac charaś cāpād iva cyutaḥ
english: "Recognising that the ocean was afraid, that foremost of demons rushed to the Himālayan forest like an arrow discharged from a bow."

sanskrit: tatas tasya gireḥ śvetā gajendravipulāḥ śilāḥ cikṣepa bahudhā bhūmau dundubhir vinanāda ca
english: "Then Dundubhi hurled many white boulders, as vast as great elephants, of that mountain to the ground and roared loudly."

sanskrit: tataḥ śvetāmbudākāraḥ saumyaḥ prītikarākṛtiḥ himavān abravīd vākyaṃ sva eva śikhare sthitaḥ
english: "Then Himavān, white as a rain-cloud, gentle, of pleasant form, standing upon his own peak, spoke:"

sanskrit: kleṣṭum arhasi māṃ na tvaṃ dundubhe dharmavatsala raṇakarmasv akuśalas tapasviśaraṇaṃ hy aham
english: "'You ought not to harass me, O Dundubhi, O devotee of dharma — I am unskilled in the deeds of battle, for I am the refuge of ascetics.'"

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā girirājasya dhīmataḥ uvāca dundubhir vākyaṃ krodhāt saṃraktalocanaḥ
english: "Hearing those words of the wise king of mountains, Dundubhi spoke, his eyes reddened with anger:"

sanskrit: yadi yuddhe 'samarthas tvaṃ madbhayād vā nirudyamaḥ tam ācakṣva pradadyān me yo 'dya yuddhaṃ yuyutsataḥ
english: "'If you are incapable of battle, or if you have no inclination out of fear of me, then name to me one who would today give battle to me who am eager to fight.'"

sanskrit: himavān abravīd vākyaṃ śrutvā vākyaviśāradaḥ anuktapūrvaṃ dharmātmā krodhāt tam asurottamam
english: "Himavān, master of speech, righteous-souled, hearing him, spoke words never spoken before to that foremost of demons in his anger:"

sanskrit: vālī nāma mahāprājñaḥ śakratulyaparākramaḥ adhyāste vānaraḥ śrīmān kiṣkindhām atulaprabhām
english: "'There is a monkey of great wisdom named Vālī, glorious and of valour equal to Indra's, who resides in Kiṣkindhā of incomparable splendour.'"

sanskrit: sa samartho mahāprājñas tava yuddhaviśāradaḥ dvandvayuddhaṃ mahad dātuṃ namucer iva vāsavaḥ
english: "'That greatly wise one, skilled in warfare, is capable of giving you great single combat, as Vāsava gave to Namuci.'"

sanskrit: taṃ śīghram abhigaccha tvaṃ yadi yuddham ihecchasi sa hi durdharṣaṇo nityaṃ śūraḥ samarakarmaṇi
english: "'Go to him quickly, if you desire battle here — for he is ever irresistible, a hero in the deeds of war.'"

sanskrit: śrutvā himavato vākyaṃ krodhāviṣṭaḥ sa dundubhiḥ jagāma tāṃ purīṃ tasya kiṣkindhāṃ vālinas tadā
english: "Hearing the words of Himavān, Dundubhi, overcome with anger, went to that city of Vālī — Kiṣkindhā."

sanskrit: dhārayan māhiṣaṃ rūpaṃ tīkṣṇaśṛṅgo bhayāvahaḥ prāvṛṣīva mahāmeghas toyapūrṇo nabhastale
english: "Wearing the form of a buffalo, with sharp horns, terrifying, he was like a great rain-cloud full of water in the sky at the onset of the monsoon."

sanskrit: tatas tu dvāram āgamya kiṣkindhāyā mahābalaḥ nanarda kampayan bhūmiṃ dundubhir dundubhir yathā
english: "Then that mighty Dundubhi, arriving at the gate of Kiṣkindhā, roared, shaking the earth like a kettledrum."

sanskrit: samīpajān drumān bhañjan vasudhāṃ dārayan khuraiḥ viṣāṇenollekhan darpāt taddvāraṃ dvirado yathā
english: "Breaking the nearby trees, tearing the earth with his hooves, scratching at that gate with his horns in arrogance, like an elephant."

sanskrit: antaḥpuragato vālī śrutvā śabdam amarṣaṇaḥ niṣpapāta saha strībhis tārābhir iva candramāḥ
english: "Vālī, who had entered the inner chambers, hearing the noise and being intolerant, burst forth with his women, like the moon with the Tārā stars."

sanskrit: mitaṃ vyaktākṣarapadaṃ tam uvāca sa dundubhim harīṇām īśvaro vālī sarveṣāṃ vanacāriṇām
english: "Vālī, lord of all the forest-ranging monkeys, spoke to that Dundubhi in measured, clear words:"

sanskrit: kimarthaṃ nagaradvāram idaṃ ruddhvā vinardasi dundubhe vidito me 'si rakṣa prāṇān mahābala
english: "'For what reason do you roar here blocking this city gate? You are known to me, O Dundubhi, O mighty one — protect your life.'"

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā vānarendrasya dhīmataḥ uvāca dundubhir vākyaṃ krodhāt saṃraktalocanaḥ
english: "Hearing those words of the wise lord of monkeys, Dundubhi spoke, his eyes reddened with anger:"

sanskrit: na tvaṃ strīsaṃnidhau vīra vacanaṃ vaktum arhasi mama yuddhaṃ prayaccha tvaṃ tato jñāsyāmi te balam
english: "'You ought not to speak in the presence of women, O hero — give me battle; then I shall know your strength.'"

sanskrit: atha vā dhārayiṣyāmi krodham adya niśām imām gṛhyatām udayaḥ svairaṃ kāmabhogeṣu vānara
english: "'Or else I shall restrain my anger for this one night — take your pleasure freely in the enjoyment of desires, O monkey.'"

sanskrit: yo hi mattaṃ pramattaṃ vā suptaṃ vā rahitaṃ bhṛśam hanyāt sa bhrūṇahā loke tvadvidhaṃ madamohitam
english: "'For whoever would slay one who is intoxicated, heedless, asleep, or utterly alone — such a one would be a slayer of an embryo in this world, one deluded by pride, like you.'"

sanskrit: sa prahasyābravīn mandaṃ krodhāt tam asurottamam visṛjya tāḥ striyaḥ sarvās tārāprabhṛtikās tadā
english: "He laughed and spoke gently with anger to that foremost of demons, having sent away all those women beginning with Tārā."

sanskrit: matto 'yam iti mā maṃsthā yady abhīto 'si saṃyuge mado 'yaṃ saṃprahāre 'smin vīrapānaṃ samarthyatām
english: "'Do not think of me as drunk — if you are fearless in battle, let this intoxication in this combat be reckoned as the warrior's drink.'"

sanskrit: tam evam uktvā saṃkruddho mālām utkṣipya kāñcanīm pitrā dattāṃ mahendreṇa yuddhāya vyavatiṣṭhata
english: "Having spoken thus and being greatly angered, he threw up the golden garland given him by his father the great Indra and stood ready for battle."

sanskrit: viṣāṇayor gṛhītvā taṃ dundubhiṃ girisaṃnibham vālī vyāpātayāṃ cakre nanarda ca mahāsvanam
english: "Seizing that Dundubhi, who resembled a mountain, by the horns, Vālī threw him down and roared with a great sound."

sanskrit: yuddhe prāṇahare tasmin niṣpiṣṭo dundubhis tadā śrotrābhyām atha raktaṃ tu tasya susrāva pātyataḥ papāta ca mahākāyaḥ kṣitau pañcatvam āgataḥ
english: "In that life-taking battle, Dundubhi was crushed; blood then flowed from both his ears as he fell, and that great-bodied one crashed to earth, reduced to the five elements."

sanskrit: taṃ tolayitvā bāhubhyāṃ gatasattvam acetanam cikṣepa vegavān vālī vegenaikena yojanam
english: "Having lifted that lifeless, unconscious body with both arms, swift Vālī hurled it a full league with a single burst of speed."

sanskrit: tasya vegapraviddhasya vaktrāt kṣatajabindavaḥ prapetur mārutotkṣiptā mataṅgasyāśramaṃ prati
english: "From the mouth of him thus hurled with force, drops of blood were carried by the wind and fell toward the hermitage of Mataṅga."

sanskrit: tān dṛṣṭvā patitāṃs tatra muniḥ śoṇitavipruṣaḥ utsasarja mahāśāpaṃ kṣeptāraṃ vālinaṃ prati iha tenāpraveṣṭavyaṃ praviṣṭasya badho bhavet
english: "Seeing those drops of blood fallen there, the sage discharged a great curse against Vālī, the thrower: 'This place must not be entered by him; if he enters, he will meet his death.'"

sanskrit: sa maharṣiṃ samāsādya yācate sma kṛtāñjaliḥ
english: "He went to the great sage and besought him with joined palms."

sanskrit: tataḥ śāpabhayād bhīta ṛśyamūkaṃ mahāgirim praveṣṭuṃ necchati harir draṣṭuṃ vāpi nareśvara
english: "Then, afraid and fearful of the curse, that monkey will not enter, nor even approach, the great mountain Ṛśyamūka, O lord of men."

sanskrit: tasyāpraveśaṃ jñātvāham idaṃ rāma mahāvanam vicarāmi sahāmātyo viṣādena vivarjitaḥ
english: "Knowing his prohibition from entry, O Rāma, I roam this great forest with my minister, free from despair."

sanskrit: eṣo 'sthinicayas tasya dundubheḥ saṃprakāśate vīryotsekān nirastasya girikūṭanibho mahān
english: "Here the heap of bones of that Dundubhi, hurled away in excess of valour, is visible — great, resembling a mountain peak."

sanskrit: ime ca vipulāḥ sālāḥ sapta śākhāvalambinaḥ yatraikaṃ ghaṭate vālī niṣpatrayitum ojasā
english: "And here are these seven great śāla trees, their branches hanging down — to strip a single one of its leaves is Vālī's feat of strength."

sanskrit: etad asyāsamaṃ vīryaṃ mayā rāma prakāśitam kathaṃ taṃ vālinaṃ hantuṃ samare śakṣyase nṛpa
english: "This incomparable valour of his has been set forth by me, O Rāma; how, O king, will you be able to slay that Vālī in battle?"

sanskrit: yadi bhindyād bhavān sālān imāṃs tv ekeṣuṇā tataḥ jānīyāṃ tvāṃ mahābāho samarthaṃ vālino vadhe
english: "If you, O mighty-armed one, were to split these śāla trees with a single arrow, then I would know you capable of slaying Vālī."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ rāghavo dundubheḥ kāyaṃ pādāṅguṣṭhena līlayā tolayitvā mahābāhuś cikṣepa daśayojanam
english: Hearing those words of the great-souled Sugrīva, the mighty-armed Rāghava effortlessly lifted the body of Dundubhi with his big toe and hurled it ten leagues.

sanskrit: kṣiptaṃ dṛṣṭvā tataḥ kāyaṃ sugrīvaḥ punar abravīt lakṣmaṇasyāgrato rāmam idaṃ vacanam arthavat
english: Seeing the body thus hurled, Sugrīva then spoke these meaningful words to Rāma in the presence of Lakṣmaṇa:

sanskrit: ārdraḥ samāṃsapratyagraḥ kṣiptaḥ kāyaḥ purā sakhe laghuḥ saṃprati nirmāṃsas tṛṇabhūtaś ca rāghava nātra śakyaṃ balaṃ jñātuṃ tava vā tasya vādhikam
english: "When it was hurled before, O friend, the body was fresh, moist and full of flesh; now, O Rāghava, it is light, desiccated, and reduced to straw — hence your strength or his, which is greater, cannot be judged from this."

sanskrit: etac ca vacanaṃ śrutvā sugrīveṇa subhāṣitam pratyayārthaṃ mahātejā rāmo jagrāha kārmukam
english: Hearing these well-spoken words of Sugrīva, the greatly resplendent Rāma took up his bow to give proof of his power.

sanskrit: sa gṛhītvā dhanur ghoraṃ śaram ekaṃ ca mānadaḥ sālān uddiśya cikṣepa jyāsvanaiḥ pūrayan diśaḥ
english: He, the honoured one, taking up the terrible bow and a single arrow, let fly at the śāla trees, filling the directions with the sound of the bowstring.

sanskrit: sa visṛṣṭo balavatā bāṇaḥ svarṇapariṣkṛtaḥ bhittvā sālān giriprasthe sapta bhūmiṃ viveśa ha
english: That arrow, adorned with gold, released by the powerful one, pierced all seven śāla trees on the mountain slope and entered the earth.

sanskrit: praviṣṭas tu muhūrtena rasāṃ bhittvā mahājavaḥ niṣpatya ca punas tūrṇaṃ svatūṇīṃ praviveśa ha
english: Having entered the earth, that swift arrow, piercing through to the netherworld, swiftly leapt back out and returned to its own quiver.

sanskrit: tān dṛṣṭvā sapta nirbhinnān sālān vānarapuṃgavaḥ rāmasya śaravegena vismayaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ
english: Seeing those seven śāla trees pierced through by the speed of Rāma's arrow, the foremost of monkeys was filled with the utmost amazement.

sanskrit: sa mūrdhnā nyapatad bhūmau pralambīkṛtabhūṣaṇaḥ sugrīvaḥ paramaprīto rāghavāya kṛtāñjaliḥ
english: Sugrīva, exceedingly delighted, his ornaments hanging loose, fell to the ground with his head and joined his palms to the Rāghava.

sanskrit: idaṃ covāca dharmajñaṃ karmaṇā tena harṣitaḥ rāmaṃ sarvāstraviduṣāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ śūram avasthitam
english: Gladdened by that feat, he spoke these words to Rāma, knower of dharma, best among all who know weapons, the steadfast hero:

sanskrit: sendrān api surān sarvāṃs tvaṃ bāṇaiḥ puruṣarṣabha samarthaḥ samare hantuṃ kiṃ punar vālinaṃ prabho
english: "You, O bull among men, are capable of slaying in battle all the gods together with Indra by your arrows — how much more then Vālī, O lord."

sanskrit: yena sapta mahāsālā girir bhūmiś ca dāritāḥ bāṇenaikena kākutstha sthātā te ko raṇāgrataḥ
english: "By whom seven great śāla trees, the mountain, and the earth have been cloven by a single arrow, O Kākutstha — who could stand before you in the van of battle?"

sanskrit: adya me vigataḥ śokaḥ prītir adya parā mama suhṛdaṃ tvāṃ samāsādya mahendravaruṇopamam
english: "Today my grief has departed, today my joy is supreme, having encountered you as my friend — you who are comparable to Mahendra and Varuṇa."

sanskrit: tam adyaiva priyārthaṃ me vairiṇaṃ bhrātṛrūpiṇam vālinaṃ jahi kākutstha mayā baddho 'yam añjaliḥ
english: "Today itself, for my dear sake, slay Vālī — who is my enemy wearing the guise of a brother, O Kākutstha; these palms are joined by me in supplication."

sanskrit: tato rāmaḥ pariṣvajya sugrīvaṃ priyadarśanam pratyuvāca mahāprājño lakṣmaṇānumataṃ vacaḥ
english: Then Rāma, the greatly wise one, embracing the pleasing-looking Sugrīva, replied with words approved by Lakṣmaṇa:

sanskrit: asmād gacchāma kiṣkindhāṃ kṣipraṃ gaccha tvam agrataḥ gatvā cāhvaya sugrīva vālinaṃ bhrātṛgandhinam
english: "Let us go from here to Kiṣkindhā — go quickly in front; and upon arriving, O Sugrīva, challenge Vālī who has only the semblance of a brother."

sanskrit: sarve te tvaritaṃ gatvā kiṣkindhāṃ vālinaḥ purīm vṛkṣair ātmānam āvṛtya vyatiṣṭhan gahane vane
english: All of them went quickly to Kiṣkindhā, the city of Vālī, and concealed themselves with trees, standing in the dense forest.

sanskrit: sugrīvo vyanadad ghoraṃ vālino hvānakāraṇāt gāḍhaṃ parihito vegān nādair bhindann ivāmbaram
english: Sugrīva roared terribly for the purpose of challenging Vālī, clothed in a tight garment, splitting the sky, as it were, with his cries in his swiftness.

sanskrit: taṃ śrutvā ninadaṃ bhrātuḥ kruddho vālī mahābalaḥ niṣpapāta susaṃrabdho bhāskaro 'stataṭād iva
english: Hearing that roar of his brother, the mighty Vālī, enraged, burst forth in great fury, like the sun from the rim of the sunset mountain.

sanskrit: tataḥ sutumulaṃ yuddhaṃ vālisugrīvayor abhūt gagane grahayor ghoraṃ budhāṅgārakayor iva
english: Then there arose a most tumultuous and terrible battle between Vālī and Sugrīva in the sky, like that of the planets Mercury and Mars.

sanskrit: talair aśanikalpaiś ca vajrakalpaiś ca muṣṭibhiḥ jaghnatuḥ samare 'nyonyaṃ bhrātarau krodhamūrchitau
english: Those two brothers, overcome with rage, struck each other in combat with palms like thunderbolts and fists like vajras.

sanskrit: tato rāmo dhanuṣpāṇis tāv ubhau samudīkṣya tu anyonyasadṛśau vīrāv ubhau devāv ivāśvinau
english: Then Rāma, bow in hand, observing both of them — those two heroes who resembled each other mutually, like two divine Aśvins —

sanskrit: yan nāvagacchat sugrīvaṃ vālinaṃ vāpi rāghavaḥ tato na kṛtavān buddhiṃ moktum antakaraṃ śaram
english: — since the Rāghava could not distinguish Sugrīva from Vālī, he did not then resolve to release the death-dealing arrow.

sanskrit: etasminn antare bhagnaḥ sugrīvas tena vālinā apaśyan rāghavaṃ nātham ṛśyamūkaṃ pradudruve
english: In this interval, Sugrīva was broken by Vālī and, not seeing the Rāghava as his protector, fled headlong to Ṛśyamūka.

sanskrit: klānto rudhirasiktāṅgaḥ prahārair jarjarīkṛtaḥ vālinābhidrutaḥ krodhāt praviveśa mahāvanam
english: Exhausted, his body drenched in blood, shattered by blows, pursued by Vālī in wrath, he entered the great forest.

sanskrit: taṃ praviṣṭaṃ vanaṃ dṛṣṭvā vālī śāpabhayāt tataḥ mukto hy asi tvam ity uktvā sa nivṛtto mahābalaḥ
english: Seeing him enter the forest, the mighty Vālī, out of fear of the curse, said 'You are freed' and turned back.

sanskrit: rāghavo 'pi saha bhrātrā saha caiva hanūmatā tad eva vanam āgacchat sugrīvo yatra vānaraḥ
english: The Rāghava too, together with his brother and also with Hanūmat, came to that very forest where the monkey Sugrīva was.

sanskrit: taṃ samīkṣyāgataṃ rāmaṃ sugrīvaḥ sahalakṣmaṇam hrīmān dīnam uvācedaṃ vasudhām avalokayan
english: Seeing Rāma arrive with Lakṣmaṇa, Sugrīva, ashamed and dejected, looking down at the earth, spoke these words:

sanskrit: āhvayasveti mām uktvā darśayitvā ca vikramam vairiṇā ghātayitvā ca kim idānīṃ tvayā kṛtam
english: "Having told me 'Challenge him,' and having displayed your prowess, and then having had me struck down by my enemy — what is this that you have now done?"

sanskrit: tām eva velāṃ vaktavyaṃ tvayā rāghava tattvataḥ vālinaṃ na nihanmīti tato nāham ito vraje
english: "At that very moment you should have told me truly, O Rāghava, 'I will not slay Vālī' — then I would not have departed from here."

sanskrit: tasya caivaṃ bruvāṇasya sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ karuṇaṃ dīnayā vācā rāghavaḥ punar abravīt
english: As the great-souled Sugrīva spoke thus with pitiable and mournful voice, the Rāghava again replied:

sanskrit: sugrīva śrūyatāṃ tātaḥ krodhaś ca vyapanīyatām kāraṇaṃ yena bāṇo 'yaṃ na mayā sa visarjitaḥ
english: "Hear me, dear Sugrīva, and let your anger be dispelled — hear the reason why that arrow was not released by me."

sanskrit: alaṃkāreṇa veṣeṇa pramāṇena gatena ca tvaṃ ca sugrīva vālī ca sadṛśau sthaḥ parasparam
english: "In ornaments, dress, build, and gait, you and Vālī, O Sugrīva, are alike to each other."

sanskrit: svareṇa varcasā caiva prekṣitena ca vānara vikrameṇa ca vākyaiś ca vyaktiṃ vāṃ nopalakṣaye
english: "In voice, in lustre, in glance, O monkey, in manner of movement, and in speech — I could not discern any mark of distinction between you two."

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ rūpasādṛśyān mohito vānarottama notsṛjāmi mahāvegaṃ śaraṃ śatrunibarhaṇam
english: "Thus, O foremost of monkeys, confounded by the similarity of form, I did not release that swift, enemy-destroying arrow."

sanskrit: etanmuhūrte tu mayā paśya vālinam āhave nirastam iṣuṇaikena veṣṭamānaṃ mahītale
english: "But see now — this very moment I shall fell Vālī in battle with a single arrow, writhing on the ground."

sanskrit: abhijñānaṃ kuruṣva tvam ātmano vānareśvara yena tvām abhijānīyāṃ dvandvayuddham upāgatam
english: "Make some distinguishing mark upon yourself, O lord of monkeys, by which I may recognise you as you come to single combat."

sanskrit: gajapuṣpīm imāṃ phullām utpāṭya śubhalakṣaṇām kuru lakṣmaṇa kaṇṭhe 'sya sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ
english: "Uprooting this blossoming gajapuṣpī creeper of auspicious marks, place it, O Lakṣmaṇa, around the neck of this great-souled Sugrīva."

sanskrit: tato giritaṭe jātām utpāṭya kusumāyutām lakṣmaṇo gajapuṣpīṃ tāṃ tasya kaṇṭhe vyasarjayat
english: Then, having uprooted from the mountain slope that gajapuṣpī laden with blossoms, Lakṣmaṇa placed it around his neck.

sanskrit: sa tathā śuśubhe śrīmāṃl latayā kaṇṭhasaktayā mālayeva balākānāṃ sasaṃdhya iva toyadaḥ
english: He, the glorious one, thus adorned with the creeper clinging to his neck, shone like a rain-cloud with the Saṃdhyā glow, like a garland of cranes.

sanskrit: vibhrājamāno vapuṣā rāmavākyasamāhitaḥ jagāma saha rāmeṇa kiṣkindhāṃ vālipālitām
english: Shining brilliantly in form, confirmed by Rāma's words, he went together with Rāma to Kiṣkindhā, governed by Vālī.
